identity: Dutch, full-time VU BSc Pharmaceutical Sciences for 2026–2027. General required core with open minor choices and no formal graduation specialisation. Adopted regulations Article 11.3 resolves differences between publicity and actual annual allocation.
ledger: Project moderne ontwikkelingen in de farmaceutische wetenschappen
Filosofie en geschiedenis van de natuurwetenschappen
Individual pharmaceutical research in a research group, assessed through practical work, a thesis and a presentation.
Students can choose a chemistry- or biology-focused minor or another approved elective package.
progression: The 2026–2027 regulations list 60 EC in each of years one and two, then 12 EC of taught requirements, an 18 EC project and 30 EC of electives. The current regulations govern exact course names and year allocations. The laboratory safety module, Dutch diagnostic or remedial language work and mentoring add no credits. The binding first-year recommendation normally requires 42 EC. The basic pharmacochemistry lab must be passed before the bioanalytical chemistry, molecular pharmacology, synthesis, molecular toxicology and molecular modelling practicals. The usual periods 5–6 project requires all first-year courses, all specified practicals including molecular modelling, and 120 EC including electives. The exceptional periods 2–3 project requires all other courses passed by 31 August of the preceding academic year. The project normally includes experimental research, a lab journal, a thesis, a talk and a poster. Four assessment categories count equally and each requires at least 5.5. The elective period normally needs approval, except for listed minors or other specified exemptions. It permits up to 6 EC at level 100 and requires at least 12 EC at level 300. Chemistry- and biology-focused minors are elective directions.
